Good evening, and welcome to the Hudson Hotel. How can I help you?
Good evening. I want to check in, please. The reservation is for Rodrigues.
Yes, Mr. Rodrigues. Four nights, a double room. Do you need two keys?
Yes, I do. And I need a quiet room, please.
No problem. Your room is on the tenth floor. The elevator is on the left.
Thank you. Do you have breakfast?
Yes, we do. Breakfast is from seven to ten, on the second floor.
Great. And what time do we check out?
At eleven. Enjoy New York!

Welcome to your room. Do you need information? Here it is. Breakfast is on the second floor, from seven to ten. The gym is on the third floor. You check out at eleven. Do you need a late check-out? Please call the front desk. For the front desk, press zero. We do not have a restaurant for dinner, but there are many restaurants on our street. Have a good night.

I travel a lot for my work, and at every hotel I ask the same three questions. First, do you have a quiet room? I don't need a big room, but I need a quiet room. Second, what time is breakfast? I like breakfast early. And third, what time do I check out? The receptionist answers, I say thank you, and I go to my room. Three questions, and my night is good.

Carlos and his wife arrive at the hotel. Carlos says: I want to check in, please. He says: I need a quiet room. The receptionist gives him two keys. He asks: Do you have breakfast? They take the elevator to the tenth floor.
